lead.headline: Oil Tops $110 as Houthi Attacks Hit Saudi Arabia
lead.deck: The US orders some diplomats and family members out of the kingdom.
body: Brent crude, the benchmark for world oil prices, rose to about $110 a barrel on Thursday 22 October, after settling at $108.82 on Wednesday. The National reported Brent up 1.7%, or $1.81, to $110.63 in early trading, and US crude (WTI) up 1.4% to $98.52. The trigger was a fresh round of attacks by the Houthis, the Yemeni group, on Saudi targets.

On Wednesday a drone attack near Shaybah, a Saudi Aramco oilfield that produces about one million barrels of crude a day, killed two people, reports said. The Saudi Energy Ministry said debris from a drone intercepted by air defences fell near a processing plant and that operations were unaffected. Hours later, an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and wounded eight, according to Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority. The Houthis had not commented on the Dammam attack.

Washington has ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure. The East-West pipeline, which has a capacity of about seven million barrels a day and carries crude from eastern fields to Red Sea terminals, is a key alternative to the Strait of Hormuz. It was reportedly halted on 5 October after a Houthi strike damaged a pumping station. Kpler data showed at least 18 attacks on shipping over the previous two weeks.

The effects reached India within hours. Indian shares fell for a third straight session on Thursday, with the Sensex down 460.30 points at 73,249.39 and the Nifty 50 at 22,687.65. HDFC Sky listed worries that dearer oil could raise inflation, widen the import bill and squeeze company margins.

lead.why: Saudi Arabia is a major oil exporter, and its alternative route around Hormuz is itself under attack. India buys much of its oil abroad, so higher prices feed into the rupee, inflation and the budget.

world.headline: Iran Says No Talks With the US Until Its Demands Are Met
world.deck: Tehran ties any dialogue to seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
body: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian told Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir, that there will be no talks with the United States until Iran's demands are met, according to Just Security's daily round-up. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf added that the US cannot regain Tehran's trust until it meets seven conditions Iran set in September for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran is also trying to position itself as a mediator in the Yemen conflict. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran has had no reply from Saudi Arabia or the Houthis to its offer to broker talks, and warned that foreign intervention would complicate matters. Separately, Araqchi said Iran is 'fully prepared to defend itself', according to Nation Thailand.

Shipping remains under threat. Kpler counted at least 18 attacks on shipping in two weeks, and LSEG analysts said Iran was targeting tankers beyond Hormuz, into the Gulf of Oman. Hormuz and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia together explain why oil sits above $110.

Regional alliances are shifting too. An AK Party lawmaker said Turkey will submit a parliamentary mandate to deploy military personnel to Saudi Arabia under its defence pact with the kingdom and Pakistan. In southern Iran, unexplained explosions were reported in Sirik on 21 October; their nature and origin are unknown, Nation Thailand reported.

world.connect: Geography: Hormuz links the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman. When it is disrupted, exporters need pipelines, such as Saudi Arabia's East-West line to the Red Sea, to reach buyers.

india.headline: Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213 Crore IPO Enters Its Final Day
india.deck: Bidding closes on 23 October; the shares are due to list on 28 October.
body: The initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, worth about Rs 30,213 crore, opened on Wednesday 21 October and closes on 23 October. The price band is Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 a share. The minimum bid is one lot of 12 shares, which is Rs 13,428 at the top of the band.

By the end of the second day the issue was 5.26 times subscribed overall, up from 3.04 times on day one, according to IPO Watch. That means bids were worth more than five times the shares on offer. Retail investors, for whom 35% of the issue is reserved, had subscribed 1.53 times. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), with a 50% quota, were at 12.44 times, and non-institutional investors, with 15%, at 5.57 times.

Trendlyne lists allotment for Monday 26 October and listing on the NSE and BSE on Wednesday 28 October. IPO Watch's page does not say whether the sale is fresh shares or existing holders selling, or how the money will be used, so the prospectus is the place to check. The share sale came on a day when the Sensex fell 460.30 points and the Nifty fell for a third session.
india.why: An IPO is how a large private company first raises money from the public. Subscription multiples show how strong demand is across investor groups.

politics_and_civics.headline: Early Voting Surges in the States That Will Decide the Senate
politics_and_civics.deck: More than 13 million ballots are in, against 9 million at this point in 2022.
body: Two weeks before the 3 November midterms, an Associated Press analysis found early voting well above 2022 levels in many states that will decide control of the Senate. More than 13 million mail-in and early in-person votes had been cast nationally, against 9 million at the same point in 2022. The midterms fill state governorships and legislatures in most states and decide whether Republicans keep their House and Senate majorities.

Texas had nearly 1 million early ballots, up 74% from about 550,000. Kansas more than doubled, to over 55,000 from 27,000. Maine rose 39%, North Carolina more than 30% and Ohio 30%, or 156,000 more ballots. Ohio had removed its mail-ballot grace period, so voters must return ballots earlier. Michigan and Georgia, whose Senate seats Democrats are defending, had high totals similar to 2022, and Iowa was down about 6%.

AP cautions that part of the rise reflects states that expanded early voting and released more data. In most competitive states where Democrats are trying to flip Republican-held seats, Republicans were a smaller share of advance voters than four years ago. Texas does not report ballots by party. NBC's tracker counted 18,154,067 early votes nationally with 12 days remaining, a different count and date from AP's. In Harris County, Texas, more than 104,600 people voted on Monday, beating the previous midterm turnout record of 63,200 set in 2018.
politics_and_civics.why: Midterms test how power is shared: states run elections, while the result decides who controls Congress. Rules such as Ohio's ballot deadline can change when and how people vote.

economics.headline: RBI Minutes: Rate Cuts Are Off the Table
economics.deck: The committee voted unanimously for a 25 basis point rise to 5.50%.
body: The Reserve Bank of India released the minutes of its October Monetary Policy Committee meeting on Wednesday 21 October. The six-member committee voted unanimously to raise the repo rate, the rate at which the RBI lends to banks, by 25 basis points to 5.50%, and changed its stance to calibrated tightening. The minutes say rate cuts are off the table for now and the next move can only be a hike or a pause.

The committee cited rising inflation and signs of price pressures spilling over into a range of goods. Headline CPI inflation is expected to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters, and core inflation is projected at 4.4% this year. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said monetary policy works mainly by curtailing 'second round effects' of supply shocks, such as wage expectations and firm-level pricing.

Markets are already feeling the squeeze. On Thursday the rupee fell about 30 paise to 94.81 against the dollar and the Sensex fell 460.30 points. HDFC Sky said some committee members indicated further hikes may be needed and the minutes flagged the growth risks of aggressive tightening. The committee meets next on 2 to 4 December.
The minutes describe geopolitical developments as challenging even though the Indian economy remains strong.

science_and_technology.headline: Ancient Proteins Link Xujiayao Fossils in China to Denisovans
science_and_technology.deck: A Nature paper says the fossils are Denisovan, not a separate species.
body: A team led by Qiaomei Fu of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing reports in Nature that fossils from Xujiayao, in Hebei Province, belong to the Denisovan lineage. Excavations from 1976 to 1979 recovered 20 human fossils there, from at least 16 individuals, dated to roughly 199,000 to 138,000 years ago.

The team drilled small holes in two specimens and identified 18 endogenous proteins. The key marker is a variant in the collagen gene COL1A2 at position 996, which changes arginine to lysine. Every Denisovan with protein or genome data carries lysine there, while Neanderthals and modern humans carry arginine.

The fossils had been grouped under a species name, Homo juluensis. The paper argues the size differences behind that name are variation within one population and that the fossils are Denisovan. The authors call the work the first morphology-based identification framework for Denisovans, 16 years after their discovery. Some outside researchers were cautious: one noted that no Denisovan cranial fossils are known that could be compared with the Xujiayao cranial fragments.

The team also compared skull, jaw and teeth features. Global Times lists a low, broad cranial vault, thick skull bones, short mastoid processes and simplified premolar chewing surfaces. The Xujiayao fossils lack facial remains. Denisovans likely lived across East and Southeast Asia from about 300,000 to 45,000 years ago.
science_and_technology.why: Protein analysis can identify fossils too old or too degraded for DNA, and a skeletal 'fingerprint' would let scientists recognise Denisovans from bones alone.

explainer.title: How an IPO works
body: A company that wants money to grow can sell shares to the public for the first time. This is an initial public offering. Buyers become part-owners, and the company receives the money if new shares are sold.

The company sets a price band, and investors bid within it. 'Subscribed 5 times' means bids were worth five times the shares on offer. After allotment, the shares list on stock exchanges such as the NSE and BSE, where prices then move with demand.

Quotas decide who gets what. In the Jio Platforms issue, 35% is reserved for retail investors, 50% for qualified institutional buyers (large institutions such as funds) and 15% for non-institutional investors. Each group can be subscribed a different number of times, which is why the overall figure and the retail figure can differ.

body: 1. What did Brent crude settle at on Wednesday 21 October?
2. Which pipeline carries Saudi crude to Red Sea terminals?

Answers. 1 (b): $108.82. 2 (a): East-West. 3 (b): seven. 4 (b): 5.50%. 5 (b): 5.26. 6 (a): more than 13 million. 7 (a): COL1A2. 8 (a): 28 October.

lead.headline: Oil Costs More After Attacks in Saudi Arabia
body: Oil rose to about $110 a barrel on Thursday. The day before it was $108.82.
A group from Yemen called the Houthis attacked targets in Saudi Arabia. Two people were killed near an oilfield, and one person was killed at an airport in Dammam.
The United States told some staff and families to leave Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia sells a lot of oil, so its supply matters to the world.

world.headline: Iran Says No Talks Yet
body: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said there will be no talks with the United States until Iran's demands are met.
Iran has seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. This is a narrow sea lane for oil ships.
Ships are under attack in the area. At least 18 attacks happened in two weeks, according to a firm called Kpler that tracks ships.
A top Iranian official said the United States cannot regain Iran's trust until it meets those seven conditions.

india.headline: A Big Share Sale Ends Soon
body: A company can sell its shares to the public for the first time. This is called an IPO.
Jio Platforms is selling shares worth about Rs 30,213 crore. Bidding opened on 21 October and closes on 23 October.
After two days, people had bid for 5.26 times the shares on offer. That means demand was high.
The price is between Rs 1,065 and Rs 1,119 a share. The shares are due to be listed on 28 October.

politics_and_civics.headline: Many Americans Vote Early
body: Americans vote in midterm elections on 3 November. These decide who controls Congress.
Many people vote early. More than 13 million have already voted. At the same time in 2022, it was 9 million.
Texas had nearly 1 million early ballots, up from about 550,000. Kansas had more than double the early votes it had in 2022.
Early votes do not tell us who will win.

economics.headline: India's Bank Raises Its Rate
body: India's central bank raised its main interest rate to 5.50%. All six members of its committee voted for it.
The bank wants to stop prices from rising too fast. It says cuts are off the table for now.
It expects inflation to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters.
Its next meeting is on 2 to 4 December. Until then, people will watch oil prices and the rupee.

science_and_technology.headline: Old Bones Get a New Name
body: Scientists in China studied two ancient bones from a place called Xujiayao. The bones are about 199,000 to 138,000 years old.
They found 18 proteins in the bones. One tiny change in a protein matched the Denisovans, a group of early humans.
So the scientists say the bones belong to Denisovans. Some other researchers are careful and want more proof.
